How to Optimize Your Website for ChatGPT, Google AI, Gemini, and Perplexity

Author
Sham Marianas Editorial Team
Published
Sat Sep 19 2026
Last updated
Sat Sep 19 2026
0 Comments
Home/Blog/AI/How to Optimize Your Website for ChatGPT, Google AI, Gemini, and Perplexity

Something's changed in how people search, and if you run a website, you've probably already felt it. Fewer clicks. Weird traffic dips even though your rankings look fine on paper. That's because a lot of your potential customers aren't typing into Google anymore, they're asking ChatGPT, Gemini, or Perplexity a question and getting a full answer without ever visiting a website.


This is the whole idea behind AI search engine optimization. It's not about abandoning SEO. It's about making sure your content is something an AI model can actually pick up, understand, and repeat back to someone as a trustworthy answer. Below, I'll walk through what that looks like in practice, using the same approach our team at Sham Marianas applies when we're building out content for clients.


So What Actually Is AI Search Engine Optimization?

Here's the short version. AI Search Engine Optimization (a lot of people just call it GEO, short for Generative Engine Optimization) means writing and structuring your site so tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity can lift information straight from it.


Old-school SEO was about competing for a spot in a list of ten links. That's still relevant, don't get me wrong. But AI search doesn't hand someone a list, it hands them one answer, stitched together from whatever sources it trusts most. If your page is vague, disorganized, or just hard to parse, the AI moves on. It'll find that same information somewhere cleaner and use that instead.


You'll also hear terms like AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) thrown around a lot lately. Honestly, the boundaries between SEO, AEO, and GEO are getting blurry, and that's fine. They're all chasing the same outcome, showing up when someone has a question, whether they're typing it into a search bar or saying it out loud to an assistant.



Why This Is Suddenly Such a Big Deal

Google's AI Overviews now sit above the regular results for a huge chunk of searches. And separately, a growing number of people just skip Google altogether and go straight to ChatGPT or Perplexity when they need an answer fast.


We've watched this play out with real clients here in the UAE. A clinic or a restaurant that used to comfortably sit on page one can basically disappear from the picture if their content wasn't built with AI comprehension in mind. It's a bit unsettling the first time you see it happen.


The upside is that fixing it isn't nearly as complicated as it sounds once you know what these models are actually scanning for.


Getting Your Website Ready for ChatGPT

ChatGPT draws from a mix of trained knowledge and, depending on the version, live browsing too. A few things genuinely move the needle here:

  1. Answer the question early, not three paragraphs in. ChatGPT tends to favour content that gets to the point almost immediately.
  2. Add schema markup. It sounds technical, but it's basically just a way of labelling your content so the model knows exactly what it's looking at, a service page, a how-to, a product listing, or whatever it is.
  3. Keep things current. Outdated stats and vague, timeless-sounding claims don't inspire much confidence. Dates, recent examples, and specific numbers do.
  4. Go deep, not just wide. One blog post about a topic rarely cuts it anymore. ChatGPT seems to lean toward sites that cover a subject from multiple angles across several connected pages.



Optimizing for Google AI Overviews

Google AI optimization isn't a total departure from classic SEO, it just adds a few extra layers on top.


Get to the Point Fast

If Google's AI Overview is going to pull from your page, it usually needs the core answer sitting somewhere in the first hundred words or so. Save the storytelling for later in the article.


Keep Your Headings Actually Organized

Clean H1, H2, and H3 structure isn't just there to make skimming easier for a reader. It also gives Google's AI clear chunks of content it can lift and drop into an overview without having to guess where one idea ends and the next begins.


Don't Skip E-E-A-T

Google's Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness guidelines carry even more weight in 2026 than they used to. Real author bios, actual sources, genuine case studies, and original photos, all of that builds the kind of trust an algorithm can't fake its way around.


Website Optimization for Gemini

Gemini works a bit differently since it's tied so closely to Google's own index and Knowledge Graph. A few things worth doing:

  1. Keep your Google Business Profile complete and matching your website exactly, this one matters a lot if you're a local business.
  2. Mention related people, places, and concepts naturally throughout your content so Gemini can connect your page into a wider web of related information.
  3. Clean up your internal linking so Gemini (and honestly, any crawler) can actually follow how your pages relate to each other.


What Makes Perplexity Different

Perplexity's SEO strategy really comes down to citations. Unlike most AI tools, Perplexity shows its sources right there in the answer, which means getting picked up here can actually send real traffic your way, not just visibility, but actual clicks.


A few things that help:

  1. Publish something original. Data, a small study, an insight nobody else has already written about a hundred times.
  2. Organize your content into clear, distinct sections, since Perplexity tends to grab specific parts of a page rather than the whole thing.
  3. Don't neglect backlinks. Perplexity still weighs authority signals in a way that feels pretty familiar if you've done traditional SEO before.


Generative Engine Optimization: Tying It All Together

Generative engine optimization is really the umbrella over everything above, SEO's next chapter, built for a world where AI generates the answer instead of just pointing to a link.


A few things worth keeping in mind:

  1. Write for the person reading it first. The algorithm comes second. AI models have gotten noticeably better at spotting content that's clearly written just to game them, and they tend to push it down, not up.
  2. Break your content into pieces that make sense on their own. Each section should feel like a complete little answer, not something that only makes sense with the paragraph before it.
  3. Real expertise still wins. Personal experience, actual data, and specific examples, none of that can really be faked, and it shows.


This is basically the exact approach we take at Sham Marianas with every piece of content we produce. It's less about outsmarting an algorithm and more about just making information easier to use for people and for AI models both.



Building an AI-Friendly Content Strategy

If you're not sure where to start, here's a simple way to approach it:

  1. Go back through your existing pages and find the ones answering common customer questions. Update them with clearer structure and current info.
  2. Add an FAQ section to your most important pages. This ties directly into Answer Engine Optimization and gives AI tools something ready-made to pull from.
  3. Use schema markup wherever it fits, FAQs, products, reviews, and local business details.
  4. Keep publishing. AI models seem to trust active, regularly updated sites a lot more than ones that haven't been touched in years.
  5. Every so often, just ask ChatGPT, Gemini, or Perplexity a question related to your industry and see if you show up. It's a quick, informal way to track how you're doing.


How to Rank in AI Search Without Sounding Like a Robot

One mistake we see constantly: businesses over-optimize until their content sounds stiff, repetitive, almost mechanical. It usually backfires too, since AI models are trained to spot exactly that kind of low-effort, keyword-stuffed writing and quietly rank it lower.


A better way to go about it is writing the way you'd actually explain something to a customer standing in front of you and then adding structure and keywords on top of that afterward, not the other way around. That's the order we follow at Sham Marianas for every project, and it's held up a lot better than chasing quick algorithm tricks.


Frequently Asked Questions


What's the actual difference between SEO and GEO?

Traditional SEO is about ranking in the list of search results. GEO is about getting your content picked up, summarized, and cited directly by AI tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity, no click required.


Does "Google AI Optimization" mean I don't need regular SEO anymore?

Not at all. AI Overviews still rely on the same crawling and indexing systems Google's always used. Solid SEO is still the foundation everything else gets built on.


How long before I see results from AI search optimization?

Most businesses notice some shift within a few weeks of restructuring content, but it usually takes two to three months to see the full effect, pretty similar to normal SEO timelines, honestly.


Can a small business actually compete for AI search visibility?

Yes, and this is genuinely good news for smaller sites. AI models often favour clear, specific, well-organized answers over sheer domain size, so a focused small business can hold its own against much bigger competitors.


Is schema markup really necessary for AI search engines?

It's strongly recommended, yes. It gives AI models a clearer signal about what your content actually is, which makes it a lot easier for them to reference accurately.


Final Thoughts

AI search isn't wiping out traditional search overnight, but it's already changing how people look for information day to day. The businesses that adjust now are writing clear, well-organized, genuinely useful content. are the ones that'll keep showing up when someone asks ChatGPT, Gemini, or Perplexity for a recommendation.
